findings.title: Neighbor-query contract is per-agent and its result shape is never defined, so the vectorized hot loop cannot be built as described
findings.description:
- **Contradiction:** Line 65 specifies "for each active agent, queries nearby neighbors". Line 33 forbids "object-by-object iteration" and line 99 forbids "Python-level per-agent branching".
- **Missing decision:** The document never says how variable-length neighbor sets are returned (ragged lists, pair/CSR arrays, padded fixed-K). Line 87 itself says this interface sets the performance ceiling.
- **Stack impact:** The stack is NumPy plus PyYAML only (`pyproject.toml:10-13`), so a ragged result forces a Python loop.
- **Evidence in code:** The existing code is what this prose produces.
  - `src/migratory/engine/tick.py:49-52` issues one `query_radius` call per agent.
  - Each force in `src/migratory/engine/flocking.py:30,65,114` loops per agent.
  - Profile lookups are per-agent Python object accesses.
- **Estimated cost:** At 10K agents with three forces, I estimate hundreds of milliseconds to seconds per tick against a 50 ms budget at 20 Hz.
- **Knock-on:** The world server's planned thread offload relies on NumPy releasing the GIL (300-arch line 78), which Python-level loops do not do.
- **Pluggability:** "Replace the strategy without touching force code" (line 87) only holds if the result shape is fixed. A sort-based NumPy hash, SciPy `cKDTree` and a GPU grid each naturally emit different shapes.
- **Fix:**
  - Define one batch query for all active agents that returns pair or CSR index arrays in canonical order.
  - Hold profile parameters as a table gathered by `profile_indices`.
  - Express forces as segment reductions over those pairs.
  - Do this before slices 102–105 add more forces on the current shape.

findings.title: State ownership is contradictory: a stateless pure function versus a register/remove/query API
findings.description:
- **Stateless vs stateful:** Line 70 says the engine is stateless and "all state lives in the arrays passed to it". Line 81 gives it "query agent state, register/remove agents", which requires the engine to hold state.
- **Hidden vs exposed layout:** Line 35 says array layout is hidden behind interfaces. Lines 64–68 and 95 pass and serialize the raw arrays, so the layout is the interface.
- **Copy vs in-place:** Line 68 "returns the updated state array" implies a functional copy. Line 99's "no dynamic allocation" implies in-place or double-buffered. The code mutates in place and returns `None` (`tick.py:20-24`).
- **Identity undefined:** The document never says whether an agent is an array index or a stable ID, nor what the removal policy is.
  - `src/migratory/engine/state.py:93-98` uses `np.delete`, which shifts every later index.
  - Any stored target, leader or pack reference would break on removal.
- **Fix:** Decide who allocates, who mutates, how agents are identified, and how removal works (swap-remove, tombstone or alive-mask).

findings.title: Three-column agent state cannot carry the behaviors the document promises
findings.description:
- **Stated state:** Line 39 defines positions, velocities and profile indices only.
- **State the behaviors need:**
  - Territorial agents need a per-agent home-range center (lines 76, 113).
  - Pack hunting needs a persistent target and pack membership (lines 75, 111).
  - Herding needs a per-agent leadership or experience attribute (lines 74, 109).
  - Hunt/rest cycles and fatigue need a per-agent mode or scalar.
- **Decisions vs forces:** "Target selection" (line 111) is a decision with memory. That conflicts with "forces, not decisions… rather than state machines" (line 41) unless discrete mode is defined as state.
- **Not a profile weight:** "Low agent count" (line 75) is a population property the engine does not control.
- **Missing:** An extensible per-agent column scheme. The document does not say who allocates those columns, given the world server allocates the arrays (300-arch line 70).

findings.title: Determinism is asserted with no mechanism
findings.description:
- **Summation order:** Float sums depend on neighbor order, so swapping spatial strategies changes results unless the contract fixes ordering. Slice 105 requires identical output across the swap.
- **Randomness:** It is never mentioned. A stateless tick needs the RNG as an explicit input. With subset evaluation it must be keyed by (tick, agent) or the stream depends on the schedule.
- **Update semantics:** Synchronous update (all forces computed from the pre-tick snapshot) is not stated.
- **Precision:** Line 95 keeps float64 internally and float32 at the serialization boundary. Replay from a snapshot, or "regions must agree from shared boundary state" (line 31), then diverges from the original run.
- **Zero-copy:** The same line asks for a zero-copy path, which a float64-to-float32 conversion is not.
- **Backends:** CPU and GPU will not agree bitwise.
- **Fix:** State the determinism level: bitwise for the same build and backend, tolerance-based otherwise.

findings.title: Subset-evaluable tick does not deliver variable-rate ticking
findings.description:
- **Timestep:** Line 64's inputs include no `dt`, and line 93 mandates a fixed timestep. An agent evaluated every 16th tick either moves at 1/16 speed or integrates with 16·dt.
- **Stability:** 16·dt reopens the stability problem line 93 raises, with force weights tuned for dt.
- **Stale neighbors:** Skipped agents hold stale positions that their neighbors read. The world server expects "interpolated positions" (300-arch line 105), but no one is assigned to write them.
- **Undecided input:** "Index array or mask" is left open. They differ on ordering and duplicates.
- **Cost today:** Every force and the integrator carry two code paths (`forces.py:67-70`, `integration.py:36-44`). The only caller passes no subset (`src/migratory_server/simulation.py:60-66`).

findings.title: Aggregates "through the same neighbor query interface" will not compose
findings.description:
- **Shape mismatch:** A neighbor query over SoA state returns indices into the agent arrays. Aggregates are not rows; they carry count and dispersion.
- **Consequence:** Supporting them changes the query result type and every force, contradicting lines 45 and 87.
- **Ownership:** The spatial index is "internal/hidden" at line 35, yet line 97 has the world server injecting aggregates into it.

findings.title: Environment interface is unspecified and "read-only" contradicts stigmergy; the tick has no output channel for events
findings.description:
- **No shape:** A per-agent point query is exactly the Python callback line 99 forbids. A batch-sampling contract is needed.
- **Writes:** Swarm agents (line 77) must deposit trail markers, which is a write. Line 47 says the interface is read-only.
- **Outputs:** The tick's only output is the state array (line 68). The world server expects behavior-driven lifecycle events such as predation (300-arch line 88), and there is no channel for them or for deposits.
- **Dependency direction:** The engine must define the environment protocol itself. The environment layer (500) sits downstream of 300 and 100, and the document does not say so.

findings.title: Inter-profile interaction model is left open and contradicts "no archetype-specific code paths"
findings.description:
- **Contradiction:** Line 29 says a new species is just a new profile. Line 91 says elk–wolf separation is "qualitatively different" and adds a combinatorial dimension.
- **No structure chosen:** The document picks neither a P×P interaction matrix nor role tags.
- **Schema growth:** The profile schema is undecided between a flat struct and per-force blocks. The flat form is already forcing every profile to set every field (`src/migratory/engine/profile.py:13-18`).
- **Radii:** A single query radius per profile cannot serve both cohesion range and flight-response range.

findings.title: Anticipated Slices drop swarm intelligence and migration, which the plan assigns here
findings.description:
- **Plan scope:** The initiative plan (001, lines 33–35) assigns "all behavioral archetypes… swarm intelligence" to initiative 100.
- **Document promises:** Lines 19, 27 and 77 promise swarm and migration.
- **Gap:** Neither appears in Anticipated Slices, and the document does not state a deferral.
- **Fix:** State the deferral and its dependency on the Environment Layer explicitly, as the slice plan already does.

findings.title: Overweight for what exists: aggregation and GPU constraints from a deferred initiative
findings.description:
- **Deferred elsewhere:** The plan places multi-resolution, aggregation and GPU in initiative 620, "deliberately deferred… need not be designed proactively" (001, lines 62–67, 97–99).
- **Cut the slice:** Move "Aggregation interface support" (line 115) and the aggregate clause of line 97 to 620.
- **Cut the GPU rules:** Reduce line 99 to "forces are bulk array-in/array-out". "No dynamic allocation" is not satisfiable in NumPy, where every expression allocates temporaries.
- **Subset parameter:** Either finish its design (see the variable-rate finding) or drop it until a caller exists.

findings.title: Undecided fundamentals: dimensionality, world bounds, numeric failure
findings.description:
This is cross-cutting: the content is absent rather than located anywhere.

- **Dimensionality:** 2D versus 3D is never stated.
  - The prototypes are one of each (lines 55–56), and line 47 mentions terrain elevation.
  - The code mixes a `DIMS` constant with hard-coded `N×2` (`forces.py:31`, `flocking.py:23`).
- **World bounds:** Behavior at the edge (wrap, reflect, steer away) is undefined. It affects neighbor queries.
- **Numeric failure:** There is no policy for it, and the project convention is to fail explicitly.
  - Coincident agents divide by zero in separation (`flocking.py:88-89`).
  - A NaN then spreads through neighbor means.
  - There is no force clamp and no non-finite check.
- **Unrecorded decisions:** Lines 85, 93 and 95 still defer layout, integrator and precision. Slice 100 already chose SoA, semi-implicit Euler and float64, so record them.

findings.title: Stale and dangling references
findings.description:
- **Dead link:** Line 122 links `200-arch.world-server-foundation.md`, which does not exist. The file is `300-arch.worldserver-foundation.md`, and line 21 calls it 300-arch.
- **Stale current state:** Line 53 says "No engine exists". `src/migratory/engine/` exists and slices 100 and 101 are marked complete.
- **Undefined term:** Line 99 cites "the BulkForce pattern", which the document never defines. It is a protocol name from `forces.py:28`.
- **Slice order:** Lines 105–107 put flocking before the spatial abstraction ("replace naive queries"), contradicting line 45. The slice plan already moved the interface into slice 100.
- **Circular derivation:** The engine's interface requirements come from the world-server document (lines 97, 122), which itself depends on this one. Frontmatter line 9 lists only the concept.
